_comment: Decks for the Phase 6 harnesses -- PHASE_06 §6.105, §6.106.
ONE definition, read by scripts/play-a-game.py and
scripts/survey-decisions.py. They must agree: the workflow is
that the survey names a decision kind nothing implements, and
then play-a-game runs THE SAME DECK without survey mode to get
the loud failure and its exact evidence. A deck the second
script has never heard of breaks that in the middle.
Not imported, because both scripts run under `python -I`, which
keeps the script's own directory off sys.path. A data file needs
no import.
WHICH DECKS, AND WHY. Each one is chosen to reach a region of
Forge's decision surface, not to be a good deck. A mono-red burn
deck never attacks, so it never reaches combat however long it
runs; a deck with no creature can never be asked to sacrifice
one. Counts are deliberately far above four: the Open Format
limit is enforced on import (OpenFormat.kt) and these decks never
go through it, and four copies of the card that reaches a branch
is how a run finishes having tested nothing.
burn        damage, targeting, and a game that ends without combat
creatures   combat: attack, block, order blockers, assign damage
mixed       both, plus triggers that want ordering
counters    planeswalker loyalty costs, and which KIND of counter
blue        counterspells (targeting the stack), draw, and putting
cards back on the library in an order
black       sacrifice as a COST, sacrifice forced on an opponent,
and choosing a card out of a revealed hand
green       searching a library, and two targets that fight
artifacts   equipment: an activated ability that attaches to a
creature you choose
modes       'choose one --', and nothing else: an X spell in
the same deck gets cast first and the run never
reaches a mode at all. Abrade's two modes need
DISJOINT targets here -- a creature that is not an
artifact and an artifact that is not a creature --
so what Forge asks for next proves which mode it
actually took
xcost       an X announced before the spell, and damage divided
among several targets
